name: Cost-Function Obfuscation via Boolean Activation
description: The problem is reframed from selecting a contiguous sub-network to assigning boolean activation states (active/dormant) to entities, with a pairwise penalty for co-activated entities. The tree structure is disguised as a "minimally cohesive" property, and the connected-subgraph requirement is redefined topologically as the inability to partition the active set into two mutually isolated non-empty subsets. Models relying on keyword matching for Steiner trees will fail to map this to a graph problem, while models that genuinely reason about the constraints will deduce that the induced subgraph must be connected, which in a tree implies finding the unique minimal spanning subtree.
